Ethnolinguistic map showing the percentage of Polish language speakers in the total population in quartile categories.

Ethnolinguistic map showing the percentage of Polish language speakers in the total population in quartile categories. Covers the central Polish territory as at end of the First World War and the adjacent regions of Eastern Europe that contain partial Polish minorities (namely--parts of Silesia, Prussia, Lithuania, Belarus, western Ukraine, and Galicia). Also shows regions partially occupied by Ruthenians (Ukrainians), White Ruthenians (Belorussians), and Lithuanians. Annotated in lower margin at right in black-ink cursive writing by a later hand: Washington, October 8th, 1918. Heavily rubber-stamped by U.S. Department of State, but no direct statement of attribution is gtiven. Manuscript: Pen-and-ink (india), watercolors, and red-ink areal lining. The map sheet has been fold-lined into quarters in the past, torn at fold line, and taped on verso. Includes legend at lower left. Available also through the Library of Congress Web site as a raster image.
